text: In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful

Praise be to God, we praise Him, we seek His help, we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in God from the evils of ourselves and the bad deeds of our deeds. Whoever God guides, none can lead him astray, and whoever He leads astray, none can guide him. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, his family, and his companions, and whoever follows them in goodness until the Day of Judgment, and may peace be upon him abundantly. As for after.

This is a summary that I summarized from my book ((Remembrance, Supplication, and Treatment with Ruqyah from the Qur’an and Sunnah)) in which I summarized the section of remembrances; To be light to carry when traveling.

I limited myself to the body of the dhikr, and contented myself with mentioning one or two sources from what was found in the original in its production. Whoever wants to know the Companion or to add more to the production should refer to the original.

I ask God Almighty, through His most beautiful names and His highest attributes, to make it pure for His noble face, and that it benefit me in my life and after my death, and that it benefit whoever reads it, or printed it, or was the cause of its publication. Indeed, Glory be to Him, He is the Grantor of that and is capable of it. May God’s blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family, his companions, and those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.
footnote: Issued in the month of Safar 1409 AH
Author: Saeed bin Ali bin Wahf Al-Qahtani

text: God Almighty said: {So remember Me, and I will remember you, and give thanks to Me, but do not disbelieve}
{O you who have believed, remember Allah often}
{And the male and female remembering God often; for them God has prepared forgiveness and a great reward.}
{And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without speaking loudly in the mornings and the afternoons, and do not be of the heedless.}
And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of the one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not remember his Lord is the example of the living and the dead

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest in the eyes of your King, the highest in your ranks, better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks and them striking your necks? They said, “Yes.” He said: “Remembrance of God Almighty.”

And he, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: God Almighty says: I am as my servant thinks of me, and I am with him when he mentions me. If he mentions me to himself, I remember him to myself, and if he mentions me in a gathering, I mention him in a group better than them, and if he approaches me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit, and if he approaches to me by a cubit, I draw near to him by a length, and if he comes to me walking, I will come to him at a trot.

On the authority of Abdullah bin Busr, may God be pleased with him, that a man said: O Messenger of God, the laws of Islam have become too much for me, so tell me something that I can cling to. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your tongue will remain moist from the remembrance of God

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever reads a letter from the Book of God will be rewarded with a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied ten times the same. I do not say: “Al-M” is a letter; But: Alif is a letter, Laam is a letter, and Meem is a letter

On the authority of Uqba bin Aamir, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out while we were in Suffah and said: Which of you would like to go out in the morning every day to Buthan or to Al-Aqiq and bring from there two heaped she-camels without sin or severing ties of kinship? We said: O Messenger of God, we would love that. He said: Doesn't one of you go to the mosque and teach, or recite two verses from the Book of God Almighty that are better for him than two she-camels, and three are better for him than three, and four are better for him than four, and their numbers are better than camels?

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever sits in a seat and does not mention God in it, there will be a reproach from God upon him, and whoever lies down in a place where God is not mentioned, there will be a reproach from God upon him.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: A people does not sit in a gathering in which they do not mention God or pray for their Prophet except that there will be a period of time for them. If He wishes, He will punish them, and if He wishes, He will forgive them.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: There is no people who rise from a gathering in which they do not remember God except that they rise up from something like the carcass of a donkey, and they will be saddened.

أذكار الاستيقاظ من النوم.section_en: Remembrance of waking up from sleep
text: Praise be to God who brought us back to life after He caused us to die* and to Him is the resurrection*
Praise be to God, who healed me in my body, restored my soul, and permitted me to remember Him.

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever falls ill at night and says when he wakes up: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. To Him belongs dominion and to Him is praise, and He is capable of all things. Glory be to God, praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is great, and there is no power or strength. There is no power except in God, the Most High, the Great. Then he supplicated: O God, forgive me, forgive him. Al-Walid said: Or he said: He supplicated, his supplication will be answered. If he stands up and performs ablution and then prays, his prayer will be accepted.

{Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, are signs for those of understanding. *Those who remember Allah, standing and sitting, and on their sides. And they think about creating the heavens and the earth. Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the torment of the Fire. And the wrongdoers have no helpers. *Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith: “Believe in your Lord.” We have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and atone for us. Our evil deeds, and we died with the righteous. * Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. You do not break your promise. * So he responded. To them is their Lord. Indeed, I will not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female, some of you from one another. So those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes and were harmed in My way, and they fought and were killed. I will certainly remit their evil deeds from them, and I will admit them to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, a reward from God, by God. With Him is a good reward * Do not be deceived by the volatility of those who disbelieve in the land * A little enjoyment, then their abode will be Hell And wretched is the resting place. *But those who fear their Lord, for them will be Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, a revelation from God and from what God is better for the righteous. * And indeed, from the People of the Book is he who believes in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been sent down to them, submissive to God who does not exchange the verses of God for a price. Only a little. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, God is quick to take account. *O you who have believed, be patient and patient, and be firm and fear God. Perhaps you will succeed}

I have turned my face to the One who created the heavens and the earth, being upright, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death belong to God, Lord of the worlds, with no partner, and by this I have been commanded, and I am one of the Muslims. I am here with You and I am pleased with You. All goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not Yours. I am in You and to You. I am blessed and exalted. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.

O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants in what they differed in. text: I ask forgiveness from God three times... O God, You are peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor.

There is no god but God alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs dominion and to Him is praise, and He is capable of all things. Oh God, there is no hinderer of what you have given and no giver of what You are prevented, and the grandfather will not benefit from you.

Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, No. 708, authenticated by Al-Albani, and in Sahih Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, No

text: Oh God, the Revealer of the Book, quick in reckoning, defeat the parties, O God, defeat them and shake them
footnote: Muslim 3/1362

ما يقول من خاف قوماً.section_en: What does he who fears a people say?
text: Oh God, grant me whatever you want
footnote: Muslim 4/2300

دعاء من أصابه شك في الإيمان.section_en: A supplication for someone who has doubts about his faith
text: He seeks refuge in God
It ends beyond doubt
He says, “I believe in God and His messengers.”
He reads the Almighty’s saying {He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Inward, and He is Knower of all things}
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 6/336 and Muslim 1/120
Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 6/336 and Muslim 1/120
Muslim 1/120
Surah Al-Hadid, verse: 3. Abu Dawud 4/329 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/962.

text: Oh God, protect me with your lawful things from your forbidden things, and make me rich with your grace than anyone else
O God, I seek refuge in You from worry and sadness, inability and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debt, and the dominance of men.
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi 5/560, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/180
Al-Bukhari 7/158

دعاء الوسوسة في الصلاة والقراءة.section_en: Dua for obsessive thoughts in prayer and reading
text: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and spit on your left (three times)
footnote: Muslim 4/1729, from the hadith of Othman bin Al-Aas, may God be pleased with him, and in it, so I did that, so God took it away from me.

دعاء من استصعب عليه أمر.section_en: A supplication for someone who finds it difficult
text: Oh God, nothing is easy except what You make easy, and You make sadness easy if You wish
footnote: Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, No. 2427 (Mawarid), and Ibn al-Sunni, No. 351. Al-Hafiz said this is an authentic hadith, and it was authenticated by Abd al-Qadir al-Arna’ut in Takhreej al-Adhkar by al-Nawawi, p. 106.

ما يقول ويفعل من أذنب ذنباً.section_en: What someone who has committed a sin says and does
text: There is no servant who commits a sin and purifies himself well, then stands up and prays two rak’ahs, then asks God for forgiveness except that God will forgive him.
footnote: Abu Dawud 2/86 and Al-Tirmidhi 2/257 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/283

دعاء طرد الشيطان ووساوسه.section_en: A prayer to expel Satan and his whispers
text: Seek refuge in God from him
The call to prayer
Remembrance and reading the Qur’an
footnote: Abu Dawud 1/206 and Al-Tirmidhi, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 1/77, and see Surat Al-Mu’minun, verses 98-99.
Muslim 1/291 and Al-Bukhari 1/151

Do not make your homes graves. Satan flees from the house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited. Narrated by Muslim 1/539. Among the things that repel Satan are the morning and evening remembrances, sleeping and waking up, the remembrances for entering and leaving the house, the remembrances for entering and leaving the mosque, and other legitimate remembrances such as reciting the Throne Verse when sleeping, and the last two verses of Surat Al-Baqarah. And whoever says there is no god but God alone, with no partner, to Him belongs dominion and to Him is praise. He is powerful over everything a hundred times, and it is a protection for him from Satan for his entire day. Likewise, the call to prayer expels Satan.

الدعاء حينما يقع مالا يرضاه أو غلب على أ.section_en: Supplication when something happens that does not please him or he is overwhelmed by it
text: God destined and did what He wanted
If a matter overwhelms you, say: God is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs
footnote: A strong believer is better and more beloved to God than a weak believer, and in every good thing, strive for what will benefit you and seek help from God and do not be helpless. If something befalls you, do not say, “If only I had done such and such,” but say, “God destined and did what He willed,” for if you do, you will open the work of Satan. Muslim 4/2052
See Takhreej Al-Adhkar by Al-Arna’ut, p. 106

تهنئة المولود له وجوابه.section_en: Congratulations to the newborn and his answer
text: May God bless what was gifted to you, and you thanked the giver, and he reached his peak, and you were blessed with his righteousness. And the congratulatory one responds to him and says: May God bless you and bless you, and may God reward you with goodness, and may God grant you the same, and reward you abundantly.
footnote: See Al-Adhkar by Al-Nawawi, p. 349, and Sahih Al-Adhkar by Al-Nawawi, by Salim Al-Hilali, 2/713.

text: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge with Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein. I seek refuge with you, with the perfect words of God, from every devil and monster, and from every evil eye.
footnote: Al-Bukhari 4/119 from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both

الدعاء للمريض في عيادته.section_en: Praying for the patient in his clinic
text: There is nothing wrong with purification, God willing
I ask God Almighty, Lord of the Great Throne, to heal you (seven times)
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 10/118

There is no Muslim servant who visits a sick person whose time has not come and says: seven times.....the hadith except that he is virtuous. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud. See Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 2/210 and Sahih Al-Jami’ 5/180.

text: He, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: If a man visits his Muslim brother, he walks in the illusion of Paradise until he sits down, and when he sits down, mercy overwhelms him. If it is in the morning, seventy thousand angels will pray over him until the evening, and if it is in the evening, seventy thousand angels will pray over him until the morning.
footnote: Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Ahmad. See Sahih Ibn Majah 1/244 and Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 1/286. It was also authenticated by Ahmad Shaker.

دعاء المريض الذي يئس من حياته.section_en: The supplication of the patient who has given up on his life
text: Oh God, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the highest companion
The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hands in the water and wiped his face with them, saying: There is no god but God. Indeed, death has its bitterness.

There is no god but God and God is great, there is no god but God alone, there is no god but God alone with no partner, there is no god but God to Him belongs the kingdom and to Him is praise, there is no god but God and there is no power or strength except in God
footnote: Al-Bukhari 7/10 and Muslim 4/1893
Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 8/144 and in the hadith the siwak
Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah and authenticated by Al-Albani. See Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/152 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/317.

text: Whoever says his last words: There is no god but God, will enter Paradise
footnote: Abu Dawud 3/190 and see Sahih Al-Jami’ 5/432

دعاء من أصيب بمصيبة.section_en: Prayer for someone who has been afflicted by a calamity
text: We belong to Allah and to Him we shall return. Oh God, reward me for my calamity and give me something better than it
footnote: Muslim 2/632

الدعاء عند إغماض الميت.section_en: Supplication when the dead person closes his eyes
text: O God, forgive so-and-so (in his name) and raise his rank among the Mahdi, and make him succeed in his successor among those who departed, and forgive us and him, O Lord of the Worlds, and make room for him in his grave and light for him in it.
footnote: Muslim 2/634

الدعاء للميت في الصلاة عليه.section_en: Praying for the dead in praying for him
text: O God, forgive him, have mercy on him, pardon him, honor his abode, widen his entrance, wash him with water, ice, and hail, purify him of sins as a white garment is purified of filth, and replace him with a better home than his home, and a better family than his family, and a better husband than his wife, and admit him to Paradise, and protect him from the torment of the grave (and from the torment of the Fire).

O God, forgive our living and our dead, our present and our absent, our young and our old, our males and our females. O God, whoever of us you make alive, let him live in Islam, and whoever of us you cause to die, let him die in faith. O God, do not deprive us of his reward and do not lead us astray after him.

Oh God, so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, is under your protection, and under your protection, and he is protected from the temptation of the grave and the torment of the Fire, and you are worthy of loyalty and truth, so forgive him and have mercy on him, for you are the Forgiving, the Merciful.

Oh God, your servant, the son of your servant, and the son of your female servant need your mercy, and you are free from his torment. If he is a doer of good, increase his good deeds, and if he is an offender, then overlook him.
footnote: Muslim 2/663
Ibn Majah 1/480, Ahmad 2/368, and see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251.
Narrated by Ibn Majah, and see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251 and narrated by Abu Dawud 3/211
It was included by Al-Hakim and authenticated by Al-Dhahabi, 1/359. See Ahkam Al-Janaiz by Al-Albani, p. 125.

الدعاء للفرط في الصلاة عليه.section_en: Praying for excessive prayers upon him
text: Oh God, protect him from the torment of the grave

If he said: O God, make him an abundance and an asset for his parents, and an answering intercessor. O God, heavyen his scales and magnify his rewards, and attach him to the good of the believers, and place him in the custody of Abraham, and protect him with your mercy from the torment of hell, and replace him with a better home than his home, and a better family than his family. O God, forgive our ancestors, our excesses, and those who preceded us in faith and did good.
Oh God, make it a blessing for us, an advance and a reward
footnote: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: I prayed behind Abu Hurairah over a boy who had never committed a sin, and I heard him say... the hadith. It was included by Malik in Al-Muwatta’ 1/288 and Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf 3/217 and Al-Bayhaqi 4/9, and its chain of transmission was authenticated by Shuaib Al-Arna’ut in his verification of Sharh Al-Sunnah by Al-Baghawi 5/357.
See: Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah 3/416 and Important Lessons for the Common Ummah by Sheikh Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Baz, may God protect him, p. 15.

Al-Hasan used to recite the Fatihah of the Book to the child and say... The hadith was narrated by Al-Baghawi in Sharh Al-Sunnah 5/357 and by Abdul Razzaq, No. 6588, and Al-Bukhari commented on it in the Book of Funerals, 65, Chapter on Reading the Fatihah of the Book at the Funeral 2/113

text: To God belongs what He takes and to Him is what He gives. Everything with Him has a set term...so be patient and seek reward
And if he says: May God reward you best, comfort you best, and forgive your dead, then that is good
footnote: Al-Bukhari 2/80 and Muslim 2/636
Al-Adhkar by Al-Nawawi, p. 126

text: In the name of God and in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God
footnote: Abu Dawud 3/314 with an authentic chain of transmission, and Ahmad with the wording, “In the Name of God,” and according to the religion of the Messenger of God, and its chain of transmission is authentic.

text: Oh God, forgive him, God make him steadfast
footnote: When the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, finished burying the dead, he would stand over him and say: Ask forgiveness for your brother and ask for steadfastness for him, for now he will be asked. Abu Dawud 3/315 and Al-Hakim authenticated it and Al-Dhahabi agreed with him 1/370.

text: Peace be upon you, people of the land, believers and Muslims, and we, God willing, will follow you [and may God have mercy on those of us who come forward and those who come back]. I ask God for good health for us and you.
footnote: Salam 2/671, and Ibn Majah, and the wording is his 1/494, on the authority of Buraydah, may God be pleased with him, and what is between the two circles from the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, according to Muslim 2/671

text: Oh God, I ask You for its goodness, and I seek refuge in You from its evil

O God, I ask You for its good, the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with.
footnote: Narrated by Abu Dawud 4/326 and Ibn Majah 2/1228. See Sahih Ibn Majah 2/305.
Muslim 2/616 and Al-Bukhari 4/76

text: Glory be to Him who glorifies the thunder with its praise and the angels with its fear
footnote: When Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, used to hear thunder, he would abandon the hadith and say:... Al-Muwatta’ 2/992, and Al-Albani said the chain of transmission is authentic and suspended.

من أدعية الاستسقاء.section_en: One of the prayers for rain
text: Oh God, give us rain that is comforting, bitter, horrific, beneficial and not harmful, sooner rather than later.
Oh God, help us, Oh God, help us, Oh God, help us
Oh God, give water to your servants and livestock, spread your mercy and revive your dead country
footnote: Abu Dawud 1/303 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/216
Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/613
Abu Dawud 1/305 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/218

text: Oh God, grant us a beneficial disaster
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 2/518

text: We were blessed by God’s grace and mercy
footnote: Al-Bukhari 1/205, Muslim 1/83

text: O God, around us and not against us, O God, on the hills, the slopes, the bottoms of the valleys, and the treetops.
footnote: Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/614

text: God is Great, O God, grant us his family with security, faith, safety, Islam, and success for what you love and are satisfied with our Lord, our Lord and your Lord, God.
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi 5/504 and Al-Darimi with his wording 1/336, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/157

text: The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is guaranteed, God willing.
Oh God, I ask you, by your mercy that encompasses everything, to forgive me
footnote: Narrated by Abu Dawud 2/306 and others, and see Sahih Al-Jami’ 4/209

It was included by Ibn Majah 1/557 from the supplication of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and it was classed as hasan by Al-Hafiz in narrating the supplications. See Sharh Al-Adhkar 4/342.

text: If one of you eats food, let him say: In the name of God. If he forgets the beginning, let him say: In the name of God, at the beginning and the end.

Whoever is fed food by God should say: O God, bless it for us and feed us with something better than it. And whoever is given milk to drink by God, let him say: O God, bless it for us and increase it for us
footnote: Narrated by Abu Dawud 3/347 and Al-Tirmidhi 4/288. See Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 2/167
Al-Tirmidhi 5/506 and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/158

text: Praise be to God who fed me this food and gave me it, without any power or strength on my part
Praise be to God, many good and blessed praises, He is neither [sufficient nor] consigned, nor can we do without Him, our Lord.
footnote: It was included by the Sunan authors, except Al-Nasa’i, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/159
Al-Bukhari 6/214 and Al-Tirmidhi with his wording 5/507

دعاء الضيف لصاحب الطعام.section_en: The guest's prayer for the host of the food
text: Oh God, bless them with what You have provided for them, forgive them and have mercy on them
footnote: Muslim 3/1626

الدعاء لمن سقاه أو إذا أراد ذلك.section_en: Pray for whoever watered it or if he wanted to
text: Oh God, feed whoever fed me and give drink to whomever gave me drink
footnote: Muslim 3/26

الدعاء إذا أفطر عند أهل بيت.section_en: Supplication when breaking the fast with a household
text: May the fasting people break their fast with you, the righteous eat your food, and the angels may pray upon you.
footnote: Sunan Abi Dawud 3/367, Ibn Majah 1/556, and Al-Nasa’i in the work of the day and the night, No. 298, and he stated that he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, says it when he breaks his fast with the family, and it was authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 2/730

دعاء الصائم إذا حضر الطعام ولم يفطر.section_en: The supplication of the fasting person if he prepares food and does not break his fast
text: If one of you is called, let him respond. If he is fasting, let him pray, and if he is not breaking his fast, let him eat. The meaning of let him pray is that he should pray.
footnote: Muslim 2/1054

ما يقول الصائم إذا سابه أحد.section_en: What does a fasting person say if someone insults him?
text: I am fasting, I am fasting
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 4/103, and Muslim 2/806

الدعاء عند رؤية باكورة الثمر.section_en: Supplication upon seeing the first fruits
text: O God, bless our fruits, bless our cities, bless our Saa’, and bless our cities.
footnote: Muslim 2/1000

text: If one of you sneezes, let him say, “Praise be to God,” and let his brother or friend say to him: “May God have mercy on you,” and if he says to him: “May God have mercy on you,” let him say: “May God guide you and set your mind at ease.”
footnote: Al-Bukhari 7/125

ما يقالُ للكافر إذا عطس فحمد الله.section_en: What is said to an infidel when he sneezes, thank God
text: May God guide you and set your mind at ease
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi 5/82, Ahmad 4/400, Abu Dawud 4/308, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 2/354.

text: May God bless you, bless you, and bring you together in goodness
footnote: It was included by the Sunan authors except Al-Nasa’i, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 1/316

دعاء المتزوج لنفسه ودعاء شراء الدابة.section_en: A married man's prayer for himself and a prayer for buying an animal
text: If one of you marries a woman, or if he buys a servant, let him say: O God, I ask you for her goodness and the goodness with which you created her, and I seek refuge in You from her evil and the evil with which you created her. And if he buys a camel, let him take the top of its hump and say something like that.
footnote: Abu Dawud 2/248 and Ibn Majah 1/617 and see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/324

الدعاء قبل إتيان الزوجة.section_en: Supplication before intercourse with the wife
text: In the name of God, O God, protect us from Satan and protect Satan from what You have provided for us
footnote: Al-Bukhari 6/141 and Muslim 2/1028

text: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan
footnote: Al-Bukhari 6/99 and Muslim 4/2015

دعاء من رأى مبتلى.section_en: A supplication from someone who sees an afflicted person
text: Praise be to God, who has spared me from what He afflicted me with, and has favored me over many of His creation
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi 5/494 and 5/493, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/153

ما يقال في المجلس.section_en: What is said in the council
text: On the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: He used to count the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in one sitting a hundred times before he rose. My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Indeed, You are the Most Forgiving, the Most Forgiving.
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi and others, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/153 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/321, and his wording is by Al-Tirmidhi.

كفارة المجلس ومايختم به المجالس.section_en: Atonement for the council and what concludes the councils with it
text: Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You
footnote: It was included by the authors of Sunan and see Sahih al-Tirmidhi 3/153, and it was proven on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, never sat in a gathering, nor recited the Qur’an, nor recited a prayer without concluding that with words.... The hadith was included by al-Nasa’i in the work of the day and the night, no. 308, and Ahmad 6/77, and it was authenticated by Dr. Farouk Hamada in his investigation of the work of the day and the night by al-Nasa’i, p. 273.

الدعاء لمن قال غفر الله لك.section_en: Pray for those who said, may God forgive you
text: And to you
footnote: Ahmed 5/28 and Al-Nasa’i in the work of the day and the night, p. 218, no. 421, edited by Dr. Farouk Hamada.

الدعاء لمن صنع إليك معروفاً.section_en: Pray for those who did you a favor
text: May God reward you
footnote: Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi No. 2035. See Sahih Al-Jami’ 6244 and Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 2/200.

ما يعصم به من الدجال.section_en: What protects him from the Antichrist
text: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Antichrist and seek refuge in God from his temptation after the last tashahhud of every prayer.
footnote: Muslim 1/555 and in a narration from the end of the cave 1/556
See Hadith No. 55 and Hadith 56

الدعاء لمن قال إني أحبك في الله.section_en: Pray for those who said, “I love you for God’s sake.”
text: I love you for whom you loved me
footnote: Narrated by Abu Dawud 4/333, and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Sunan Abi Dawud 3/965

الدعاء لمن عرض عليك ماله.section_en: Pray for the one who offered you his money
text: May God bless you, your family and your money
footnote: Al-Bukhari Al-Fath 4/88

الدعاء لمن أقرض عند القضاء.section_en: Pray for those who lent when they make up for it
text: May God bless you, your family and your wealth. The reward of the predecessors is only praise and performance
footnote: It was included by Al-Nasa’i in the work of the day and the night, p. 300, and Ibn Majah 2/809. See Sahih Ibn Majah 2/809 and see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/55.

دعاء الخوف من الشرك.section_en: A supplication for fear of polytheism
text: Oh God, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You while I know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know
footnote: Ahmad 4/403 and others. See Sahih Al-Jami’ 3/333 and Sahih Al-Targheeb wa Al-Tarheeb by Al-Albani.

الدعاء لمن قال بارك الله فيك.section_en: Pray for those who said God bless you
text: May God bless you
footnote: Narrated by Ibn al-Sunni, p. 138, no. 278. See al-Wabel al-Sayyib by Ibn al-Qayyim 304, edited by Bashir Muhammad Uyun.

دعاء كراهية الطيرة.section_en: A supplication for hatred of tira
text: Oh God, there is no bird except your bird, there is no good except your good, and there is no god other than you
footnote: Ahmad 2/220, Ibn al-Sunni, No. 292, and Al-Albani authenticated it in Al-Hadith al-Sahih 3/54, No. 1065. As for omens, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was impressed by omens. That is why he heard a good word from a man and he liked it, so he said: We took your wisdom from among you, Abu Dawud and Ahmad, and it was authenticated by Al-Albani in Al-Sahih 2/363, according to Abu Al-Sheikh in the morals of the Prophet.

text: In the name of God. Thank God. {Glory be to Him who has subjugated this to us, and we were not to it. * And indeed, to our Lord we will return} Praise be to God, praise be to God, praise be to God, God is great, God is great, God is great, Glory be to You, O God, I have wronged myself, so forgive me. No one can forgive sins except you
footnote: Abu Dawud 3/34, Al-Tirmidhi 5/501, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/156

text: God is great, God is great, God is great. {Glory be to Him who has subjugated this to us, and we have not been able to abide by it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return} Oh God, we ask you in this journey of righteousness and piety, and of deeds that you are pleased with. Oh God, make this journey easy for us and long. On our behalf after him, O God, You are the companion on the journey and the successor to the family. O God, I seek refuge in You from the troubles of travel, the gloom of the scene, and the bad turn in money and family, and when he returns, he says them and adds to them, “Repentant, worshipers, to our Lord, praiseworthy.”
footnote: Narrated by Muslim 2/978

دعاء دخول القرية أو البلدة.section_en: A supplication for entering a village or town
text: O God, Lord of the seven heavens and what they overshadow, Lord of the seven earths and what they darken, Lord of the devils and what they have led astray, Lord of the winds and what they spread. I ask You for the good of this village, the good of its people, and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people, and the evil of what is in it.
footnote: Al-Hakim authenticated it, Al-Dhahabi agreed with him 2/100, Ibn Al-Sunni, No. 524, and Al-Hafiz classed it as hasan in Takhreej Al-Athkar 5/154. Ibn Baz said: Al-Nasa’i narrated it with a good chain of transmission. See Tuhfat Al-Akhyaar, p. 37

text: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. To Him belongs dominion and to Him is praise. He gives life and causes death. He is living and does not die. In His hand is goodness, and He is capable of all things.
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi 5/491, Al-Hakim 1/538, and it was authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah 2/21 and in Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/152

الدعاء إذا تعس المركوب.section_en: Pray if the boat is miserable
text: In the name of God
footnote: Abu Dawud 4/296 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 3/941

دعاء المسافر للمقيم.section_en: The traveler's prayer for the resident
text: I entrust you to God, whose deposits are never lost
footnote: Ahmad 2/403 and Ibn Majah 2/943 and see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/133

دعاء المقيم للمسافر.section_en: A resident's prayer for a traveler
text: I entrust to God your religion, your honesty, and the conclusions of your work
May God grant you piety, forgive your sins, and facilitate goodness for you wherever you are
footnote: Ahmad 2/7 Al-Tirmidhi 5/499 and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/155
Al-Tirmidhi, and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/155

text: Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: When we ascended, we would say “Allahu Akbar,” and when we descended, we would say “Allahu Akbar.”
footnote: Al-Bukhari Al-Fath 6/135

دعاء المسافر إذا أسحر.section_en: The traveler's supplication when he is enchanted
text: He hears and hears, praise be to God and His good affliction upon us, our Lord, our friend, and bestow upon us, we seek refuge in God from the Fire.
footnote: Muslim 4/2086, and the meaning of “Sam’a-Sami’” is: that is, “a witness that bears witness to our praise to God Almighty for His blessings and good tribulations.” The meaning of “He heard” is: “He who heard me conveyed this statement of mine to others and said the same as a reminder of the remembrance of magic and supplication.” And his saying: Our Lord is our friend and best upon us: meaning, protect us, protect us, and nourish us, and bestow upon us with Your abundance of blessings, and avert from us all harm. Sharh al-Nawawi 17/39.

الدعاء إذا نزل منزلا في سفر أو غيره.section_en: Supplication when it comes down to earth while traveling or elsewhere
text: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He created
footnote: Narrated by Muslim 4/2080

text: He says three takbirs for each honor, then says: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, to Him belongs dominion, to Him is praise, and He is capable of all things. They are steadfast, repentant, worshipers, to our Lord, praising God. God has been true to his promise, and he has given victory to his servant, and he has defeated the parties alone.
footnote: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say it when he returned from a campaign or Hajj. Al-Bukhari 7/163 and Muslim 2/980.

ما يقول ويفعل من أتاه أمر يسره أو يكرهه.section_en: What someone who comes to him says and does is something he likes or dislikes
text: If a matter came to him that pleased him, he, peace and blessings of God be upon him, would say: Praise be to God, by whose grace good deeds are accomplished. And if a matter came to him that he hated, he would say: Praise be to God in every situation.
footnote: It was included by Ibn al-Sunni in “Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laila” and al-Hakim and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih al-Jami’ 4/201.

فضل الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.section_en: The virtue of praying for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace
text: May God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Whoever prays a prayer for me, may God bless him ten times
And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Do not make my grave a feast, and pray for me. Your prayers will reach me wherever you are
And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: The miserly is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not pray for me
He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Indeed, God has angels traveling on earth, conveying peace to my nation.”
He, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: “No one greets me except that God returns my soul to me until I return his greeting.”
footnote: Narrated by Muslim 1/288
Abu Dawud 2/218 and Ahmad 2/367 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 2/383
Al-Tirmidhi 5/551 and others. See Sahih Al-Jami’ 3/25 and Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/177.
Al-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim 2/421 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Al-Nasa’i 1/274
Abu Dawud, No. 2041, and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/383

text: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another, or I will not guide you to anything that if you do it you will love one another, spread peace among yourselves.
Whoever combines three of them has combined faith: being fair to yourself, offering peace to the world, and spending out of frugality

On the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both: A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which Islam is best. He said: You give food and greet those you know and those you do not know.
footnote: Muslim 1/74 and others
Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 1/82 on the authority of Ammar, may God be pleased with him, with a suspended report
Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 1/55 and Muslim 1/65

كيف يرد السلام على الكافر إذا سلم.section_en: How can peace be returned to an infidel if he greets him?
text: If the People of the Book greet you, say: And upon you
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 11/42, and Muslim 4/1705

دعاء صياح الديك ونهيق الحمار.section_en: Prayers for the crow of a rooster and the braying of a donkey
text: If you hear a rooster crow, ask God for His bounty, for it has seen an angel, and if you hear a donkey braying, seek refuge in God from Satan, for it has seen a devil.
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 6/350, and Muslim 4/2092

دعاء نباح الكلاب بالليل.section_en: Supplication for dogs barking at night
text: If you hear dogs barking and donkeys braying at night, seek refuge in God from them, for they see what you do not see.
footnote: Abu Dawud 4/327 and Ahmad 3/306 and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud 3/961

text: He, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: O God, whichever believer you insult, make that bring him closer to You on the Day of Resurrection.
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 11/171 and Muslim 4/2007 and his wording, so make it a zakat and mercy for him.

ما يقول المسلم إذا مدح المسلم.section_en: What does a Muslim say if he praises a Muslim?
text: He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: If one of you is inevitably praising his friend, he should say: I think so-and-so and God is his judge, and I do not praise anyone above God. I think he - if he knows that - is such-and-such.
footnote: Narrated by Muslim 4/2296

ما يقول المسلم إذا زكي.section_en: What does a Muslim say if he is pure?
text: Oh God, do not hold me accountable for what they say, and forgive me for what they do not know [and make me better than they think]
footnote: Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, No. 761, and its chain of transmission was authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, No. 585, and what is between the two brackets is an addition by Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman 4/228 from another path.

كيف يلبي المحرم في الحج أو العمرة.section_en: How does a Mahram perform the Talbiyah during Hajj or Umrah?
text: Here you are, O God, here you are, here you have no partner. Here you are. Indeed, praise and blessings are yours and dominion, you have no partner.
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 3/408, and Muslim 2/841

التكبيرة إذا أتي الركن الأسود.section_en: Takbir when the black corner comes
text: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated the Kaaba on a camel. Whenever he came to the corner, he pointed to it with something he had and said “Allahu Akbar.”
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 3/476, and what is meant by a beautiful thing see: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 3/472

الدعاء بين الركن اليماني والحجر الأسود.section_en: Supplication between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone
text: {Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire}
footnote: Abu Dawud 2/179, Ahmad 3/411, Al-Baghawi in Sharh Al-Sunnah 7/128, and Al-Albani classed it as hasan in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/354, and the verse is from Surat Al-Baqarah, 201

دعاء الوقوف على الصفا والمروة.section_en: The supplication of standing on Safa and Marwa
text: When he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, approached Al-Safa, he recited: {Indeed, Al-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the rituals of God}. I begin with what God began with, so he began with Al-Safa and moved on it until he saw the House and faced the Qiblah, so he united and glorified God and said: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is capable of all things. There is no god but God alone. He has accomplished. He promised him, supported his servant, and defeated the parties alone, then called in between. He said something like this three times in the hadith, so he did on al-Marwah what he did on al-Safa
footnote: Muslim 2/888

الدعاء يوم عرفة.section_en: Supplication on the day of Arafat
text: The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of Arafat, and the best of what I and the prophets before me said: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is capable of all things.
footnote: Al-Tirmidhi and it was authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/184, and in Al-Hadith Al-Sahihah 4/6

text: May the peace and blessings of God be upon him, he rode Al-Qaswa’ until he came to Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram and faced the Qiblah (so he called him, and glorified him, and glorified him, and glorified him alone), and he remained standing until he reached a very high speed, so he pushed off before the sun rose.
footnote: Muslim 2/891

التكبيرة عند رمي الجمار مع كل حصاة.section_en: Takbeer when throwing stones with each pebble
text: He says “Allahu Akbar” whenever he throws a pebble at the three Jamarat, then he goes forward and stands, supplicating facing the Qiblah, raising his hands after the first and second Jamarat. As for Jamarat al-Aqaba, he throws it and says “Allahu Akbar” at each pebble and then leaves and does not stop there.
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 3/583 and 3/584, and see his wording there. Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 3/581, and it was also narrated by Muslim

ما يقول عند التعجب والأمر السار.section_en: What he says when he is surprised and happy
text: Praise God
Allah is great
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 1/210, 390, 414 and Muslim 4/1857
Al-Bukhari Al-Fath 8/441 and see Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 2/103 and 2/235 and Musnad Ahmad 5/218

ما يفعل من أتاه أمر يسره.section_en: What the one who comes to Him does is something that pleases Him
text: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him with something that pleased him or pleased him, he would fall down prostrating in gratitude to God, Blessed and Most High.
footnote: It was narrated by the Sunnis except Al-Nasa’i. See Sahih Ibn Majah 1/233 and Irwa’ al-Ghaleel 2/226

ما يقول من أحس وجعاً في جسده.section_en: What someone who feels pain in his body says
text: Place your hand on the part of your body that is hurting and say: In the name of God, three times and say seven times: I seek refuge in God and His power from the evil of what I find and I beware.
footnote: Muslim 4/1728

دعاء من خشي أن يصيب شيئاً بعينه.section_en: A supplication for someone who fears that something specific will happen to him
text: If one of you sees from his brother, or from himself, or from his wealth, something that he likes [let him pray for blessing for him], for the evil eye is valid.
footnote: Musnad Ahmad 4/447, Ibn Majah and Malik, and authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Al-Jami’ 1/212. See the investigation of Zad Al-Ma’ad by Al-Arna’ut 4/170

ما يقال عند الفزع.section_en: What to say when you panic
text: There is no god but God
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 6/181, and Muslim 4/2208

ما يقول عند الذبح أو النحر.section_en: What is said when slaughtering or slaughtering?
text: In the name of God and God is great [Oh God, from you and to you] Oh God, accept from me
footnote: Muslim 3/1557 and Al-Bayhaqi 9/287 and Ma’in al-A’aquf by Al-Bayhaqi 9/287 and others, and the last sentence I quoted in the meaning from Muslim’s narration

ما يقول لرد كيد مردة الشياطين.section_en: What does he say to the response of the devil’s mercenary kid?
text: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God, which neither the righteous nor the immoral can pass over, from the evil of what He created, acquitted, and spread, and from the evil of what descends from the sky, and from the evil of what ascends therein, and from the evil of what He spreads on the earth, and from the evil of what emerges from it, and from the evil of the temptations of night and day, and from the evil of every Tariq except one who knocks with goodness, O Most Merciful.
footnote: Ahmad 3/419 with a Sahih chain of transmission and Ibn al-Sunni, number 637, and its chain of transmission was authenticated by Al-Arna’ut in his narration by Al-Tahawiyyah, p. 133, and see Majma’ Al-Zawa’id 10/127

text: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.
And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, repent to God, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever says: I ask forgiveness from God the Great, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Ever-Subsisting, and I repent to Him, God will forgive him, even if he fled from the battlefield.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: The closest thing to the Lord to the servant is in the middle of the last night. If you can be among those who remember God in that hour, then be.
And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The closest thing a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so supplicate often
He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My heart is tempted, and I ask God for forgiveness a hundred times a day
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 11/101
Muslim 4/2076

It was included by Abu Dawud 2/85, Al-Tirmidhi 5/569, Al-Hakim and he authenticated it, Al-Dhahabi agreed with him 1/511, and Al-Albani authenticated it. See Sahih al-Tirmidhi 3/182 and Jami’ al-Usul li-Ahadith of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, 4/389-390, verified by Arna’ut.
Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i 1/279 and Al-Hakim. See Sahih Al-Tirmidhi 3/183 and Jami’ Al-Usul, verified by Al-Arna’ut 4/144.
Muslim 1/350

Narrated by Muslim 4/2075. Ibn al-Atheer said: (My heart will be tempted), that is, to be covered and obscured. What is meant is: forgetfulness. Because he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was still in the process of increasing remembrance, closeness, and constant monitoring. If he neglected to do any of it at some times, or forgot, he considered it a sin against himself, so he panicked and sought forgiveness. See Jami’ al-Usul 4/386

فضل التسبيح والتحميد ، والتهليل ، والتكب.section_en: The virtue of glorifying, praising, and glorifying God
text: He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever says Glory be to God and praise be to Him one hundred times a day, his sins will be forgiven, even if they were like sea foam.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever says: There is no god but Him alone, without partners, to Him belongs dominion, to Him is praise, and He has power over all things ten times over. It was as if he freed four people from the descendants of Ishmael

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, Glory be to God the Great.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Because I say, Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is great, I am more beloved to me than what the sun rises upon.

He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is any of you incapable of earning a thousand good deeds every day? A questioner from those sitting with him asked him: How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds? He said: He recites one hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are recorded for him or a thousand sins are removed from him
Whoever says, Glory be to God the Great, and praise be to Him, a palm tree will be planted for him in Paradise

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah bin Qais, shall I not direct you to one of the treasures of Paradise? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Say: There is no power nor strength except in God

He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most beloved speech to God is four: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is great. It does not matter to you which one you start with.

A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Teach me words to say: He said, “Say, ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner. God is great, great, and praise be to God greatly. Glory be to God, Lord of the worlds. There is no power nor strength except in God, the Mighty, the Wise.’ He said, ‘So these are for my Lord, so what is mine?’” He said: Say: O God, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, and provide for me

If a man converted to Islam, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, taught him to pray and then commanded him to pray with these words: O God, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, pardon me, and provide for me.
The best remembrance is there is no god but Allah
The remaining good deeds: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is great, and there is no power nor strength except with God.
footnote: Al-Bukhari 7/168 and Muslim 4/2071, and see: The virtue of one who says it a hundred times in the morning and in the evening.

Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 11/213 and Muslim 4/2076

كيف كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسبح ؟.section_en: How did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swim?
text: On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, holding the tasbih with his right hand.
footnote: It was included by Abu Dawud with wording 2/81 and Al-Tirmidhi 5/521. See Sahih Al-Jami’ 4/271 no. 4865.

من أنواع الخير والآداب الجامعة.section_en: One of the types of goodness and universal etiquette
text: When it is the cover of night - or evening - restrain your children; The devils spread out at that time, so when an hour of the night has passed, leave them alone, close the doors, and mention the name of God. Satan does not open a closed door, so lie down close to you and mention the name of God, cover your utensils and mention the name of God, even if you offer something to them, and extinguish your lamps.
footnote: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath 10/88 and Muslim 3/1595
